note: One scene and three follow-up edits, each with an exact answer the checker can measure. Meters, Y up, the user sits at +Z. Both arms get the same words; only 'where' differs.

where.plain: Write it as scene.mjs in this folder: its default export is a function taking no arguments that returns a three.js Object3D holding one named Mesh per part (three is installed; import it from 'three'). Name each mesh exactly as the part is named below. Node can import scene.mjs, so check your work by running it.
where.sleipnir: Build it in a new Environment called "Bench", using the instructions in .claude/commands/sculpt.md. Name each part exactly as it is named below.

stages.name: build
stages.prompt:
Model a laptop on a desk. Y is up, the floor is Y = 0, the user sits toward +Z, and everything is centered on X = 0 and Z = 0.
- "Desk top": 1.2 wide (X), 0.6 deep (Z), 0.03 thick, its top surface at Y = 0.75.
- "Leg 1", "Leg 2", "Leg 3", "Leg 4": each 0.05 × 0.05 in plan, from the floor up to the underside of the desk top, flush with the desk top's four corners.
- "Laptop base": 0.34 wide, 0.24 deep, 0.015 thick, resting on the desk, centered.
- "Lid": the same 0.34 × 0.24 footprint, 0.008 thick, hinged along the back top edge of the base (Y = 0.765, Z = -0.12). Its opening angle is 110°, where 0° is closed flat on top of the base and 90° is straight up; so it leans 20° back, away from the user. The back edge of the lid's inner face (the face that touches the base when closed) lies on the hinge line.

stages.name: thicker lid
stages.prompt: Make the Lid 0.012 thick. It grows outward: its inner face and the hinge stay exactly where they are.

stages.name: open further
stages.prompt: Open the Lid 20° further about its hinge, so its opening angle is 130°.

stages.name: move laptop
stages.prompt: Move the whole laptop (Laptop base and Lid together) 0.2 toward -X. The desk stays where it is.
